reading_candidates: Orientation: GF is generically finite, not a generically finite morphism or classical basepoint-free FS system.
Characteristic-zero failure of the Frobenius subalgebra property is possible, not universal; powers can still descend special coefficients.
A multiplicative sandwich alone does not force its limit to be kappa^{-1} psi; it only fails to squeeze to the desired value.
Positive-characteristic whole-psh reflection also uses varying-class decreasing closure; table must distinguish GF conversion from full reflection.
Earlier normal-case birational/finite conclusions are not inherently consequences of the normal EP theorem; their hypotheses and carrier scopes must be mapped accurately.
Earlier normal-case results are inapplicable to a nonnormal target, not inherently circular inputs to unibranch assembly.
Raw F_n need not be monotone; an arbitrary particular presentation can nevertheless produce a monotone family.
Closure imports include positive scaling and the structural corollary uses maxima and fixed-class limits.
A normal source in a finite birational map is the normalization; unibranchness in the structural proposition should be explained.
Some individual coefficients do descend; nonseminormality does not prohibit descent of every coefficient.
Nodal ring embedding sends x to t^2-1 and y to t^3-t; y/x is a rational inverse.
Seminormality proof must handle zero values before division.
Roberts–Singh does not apply to the node as an extension; selected elements can still admit additive-power systems.
Branch separation needs an explicitly normalized logarithm in an integral ample class.
Avoid unneeded topological-homeomorphism and projective indistinguishability claims about node versus cusp.
General Roberts–Singh systems already have fixed coefficients. Exponent zero removes the extra exponent shift; it does not mean coefficient independence.
Two-gap minimality also excludes p=0 explicitly.
Cusp polynomial formulas with m=0 must avoid negative powers and require a separate a_0=1 clause.
After forming a full identity, the two grading projections commute. The forbidden operation is truncating correction terms, not exchanging these projections.
Frame covariance transports one chosen local system; independently chosen chart systems do not automatically glue.
Additive sandwich error O(1/n) is pointwise at finite Gauss weight, not a uniform absolute error over an unbounded analytic cone.
Grouped construction supplies a weaker multiplicative bracket; it does not force convergence to s^{-1} psi.
Gauss multiplicativity proof treats infinite-weight cases first; ideal-power n=0 needs its unit-ideal convention.
Clear weights with a positive integer q so section tensor powers exist.
Distinguish frames of nu*(mL) from their qth powers framing nu*M.
Different cover sections can lie in different ample powers; take a common multiple after selecting a finite cover.
Generic weighted section has polynomial formal variables with coefficients in global sections, not a literal coefficient ring Z assertion.

Same twist and same dense-open restriction give identical global extensions on integral Y. Structured extension guarantees existence and global containment; it does not yield different extensions elsewhere.
Growing twist discussion assumes a maintained sandwich; nonzero ample class requires positive dimension.
The cusp cutoff S depends on chosen tau; t^2 needs S=2 in the two-gap case, while other tau may need less.
A coherent quotient need not have finite length in higher dimension; length bounds require an Artinian scope.
A lower ideal containment does not survive arbitrary changes to the construction.
Characteristic-zero identity failure is witnessed by the cusp, not every subintegral extension.
Monotonization need not always force exponential sparsity; C=0 and other rational schedules differ.
After positive scaling, approximant classes need not be larger than L; the worked curve example itself lies below L.
Failure of this proof to produce a GF bijection is not a counterexample to GF surjectivity.
Class promotion changes ambient presentations without changing functions; original M_i need not literally equal nu*L_i.
Regularization and assembly are arbitrary nets, not sequences.
All-characteristics proof shares elementary psh calculus and decreasing closure as well as topological and promotion inputs.
Dependency ledger imports GF regularization without needing normality.
Cusp fixed correction section can extend with R=0, but R=1 remains a legitimate convenient choice; compute in its correct bundle frame.
Worked monotonization recurrence uses n_{j+1}, consistent with the stated threshold; selected 4,12,28 sequence still works.
Cusp modified f_1=t has qth power already downstairs; residual correction obstruction comes from f_2=2+t.
Normal cone semigroup is saturated in its Veronese group lattice, with nonnegative coordinates.
Semigroup-membership notation must not append a second variable w already included.
RS gap computation on homogeneous ring extends to degree-zero charts after homogeneous localization; show z and w charts or reuse explicit computations.
Compute dimension of global H^0(O(1)) via the hypersurface or rational-normal-cone section description, not graded degree-one dimensions alone.
Quotient along cone line is locally free from both z and w charts; one chart alone does not prove global invertibility.
No impossibility claim about direct psh arguments on the nonnormal surface.
Necessity of unibranchness for EP is separate from failure of psh pullback surjectivity.
A presentation-dependent quoted theorem does not prove no presentation-independent bounds exist.
The conductor always annihilates B/A by definition; distinguish this from bounds for chosen cutoff sections.
Remove exact supplied-source numbering and novelty claims about an unavailable archive.
Remove unsupported claims of no earlier analytic application or no unified argument.
Ideal integral closure preserves semivaluation values; equal values need not be asserted to characterize integral closure without further scope.
Characteristic-p theorem gives bijection of functions, not presentations.
Appendix A exact exponent-zero explanation needs a scoped terminology correction alongside Chapter 44.

The grouped example loses the stronger mixed ideal containment, but singleton containments still give the same additive Gauss-weight estimate. Explicitly prove n W(a) <= W(Kgrp) <= (n+2) W(a), rather than claim the reflection theorem fails.
Failure to invert multinomials blocks this characteristic-zero proof, not the local sandwich conclusion in every positive-characteristic extension.
The full generic combination is needed for the stated strong ideal sandwich, not proved necessary for all valuative descent constructions.
